rows.text: Mother, I have returned.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Bronya! I thought... I thought I'd lost you.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Where were you? A—Are you hurt? I'll fetch the butler right away—
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: No, there's no need! I don't want to see Sebas right now. Sorry, mother...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I'm fine, really. I just got into a few skirmishes down in the Underworld, but nothing I couldn't handle.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The Underworld? Oh... I see.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: We may as well tell the long and short of it from start to finish.
We may as well cut to the chase and make a long story short.
In that case, report everything you saw, Commander Bronya.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: After the failed pursuit at Backwater Pass, the wanted outsiders and I were somehow taken to the Underworld.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Because of the difficult situation we were in, we formed a temporary alliance to help the residents of the Underworld resolve a few... issues of survival.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: We also defeated an ancient robot known as "Svarog," and learned some truths... about the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...I'm listening. Go on.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Madam Cocolia, it is my firm belief that the visitors from beyond the sky are not the villains we had imagined before.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I witnessed them take up arms in the name of justice, and risk their lives for the sake of others. I can also ascertain that they did come for the Stellaron, but only to relieve the disaster it has brought upon Belobog.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Mother... you've always known the truth about the Stellaron, haven't you? The responsibility of bearing that truth will fall upon me one day. Such is the burden of being guardian — to carry these secrets for eternity.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: So... I ask you to forgive my defiance, but I believe that the order to dispatch the outsiders was a mistake. To solve the problems brought on by the Stellaron, the Architects waited hundreds of years, and those outsiders may be the... the—
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Enough!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Arrogant, ignorant... Oh you disappoint me, Bronya.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: You merely glimpsed the tip of the iceberg and now you think you know everything. You spend a short time with that Underworld scum, and suddenly you have the audacity to question my orders?
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Guards! Take Bronya—
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: —They are not scum!
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: My entire life, everything you ever kept from me... I remember it clearly now. This time... this time I'm standing my ground, Madam Guardian! And please, stop dismissing me with vague excuses.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Tell me what you have seen. What exactly it is you are hiding... Why do you send the Silvermane Guards to die in the Fragmentum? Why have you abandoned the people of the Underworld? And why... why did you have that sudden change of mind?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...I see.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: I knew this moment would come sooner or later... I just didn't expect it would be so soon.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: You want to know why I gave those orders... is that right? Do you believe you are ready to learn the truth?
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Yes. I am ready... Mother.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Then come with me, Bronya.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: It is time you heard it... the voice of this dying world.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Ah, we're finally back! ...I forgot what fresh air tasted like... Nom, nom, nom.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Where do we go now?
What flavor is it?
Aren't we missing something?
Wait! I haven't finished yet... Alright, let's go.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Freedom... Cold... Mainly cold actually. Let's go.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Come... Come...
No.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Where's Sampo...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Nope. Next question.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Where's our next stop? We should find somewhere to put our feet up, as long as it's not Goethe Hotel again...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Classic unreliable Sampo — he probably guessed we'd ask where his hiding place was. No sooner are we back in the Administrative District than he sneaks off.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: We should hide in plain sight. To the hotel!
A friend in need is a friend indeed. Let's find Landau!
Home is where the heart is. Back to the Express!
No way! The boss will recognize us, plus Silvermane Guards are stationed nearby. We'd be offering ourselves up on a silver platter!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The bro or the sis? If you're talking about Gepard, we should be careful... He's a top Silvermane Guard — he'd probably get a medal for every one of us he brought in.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Where's your sense of loyalty!? Uh, that would be nice though...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Dan Heng, what do you think?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I think it'd be best to pay a visit to Serval Landau.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: So you think we should avoid Gepard for the time being, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He's an elite officer of the Silvermane Guards. It wouldn't be easy to get to him. Besides... if he hasn't been persuaded by Bronya's letter, we'd be walking right into the lion's den.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hmm, makes sense... Guess we better head over to Serval's workshop then?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Mm. But... we must keep a low profile — we're still wanted fugitives.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What's wrong, Seele?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Nothing, it's just a little... new.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: The last time I was on the surface, I was still a child. I have no memory of any of this.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: The Overworld and the Underworld... We've... We've been cut off for so long.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I'm okay. Let's go.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: There are so many Silvermane Guards on patrol. Is it usually like this?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No, I don't remember the security being this tight last time... It might have something to do with us.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The supreme guardian has probably learned of our arrival already. Bronya...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Who is it? Shop's closed today, you'll have to come back tomorrow!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: It's the radiator fixers.
It's a big customer with bigger pockets!
Hah...?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Ha, not interested — I need time, not money!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Serval! We came past here before and helped you fix a few things, remember?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What...?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Ah, I remember! The three outsiders! Wait — why are you still strolling around the city? Do you know the Silvermane Guards are looking all over for you?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Quick, act natural and get inside. Don't get spotted!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Alright, you'll be safe here. My workshop has pretty good soundproofing, and barely anyone comes in.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Just what crime did you commit exactly? They recalled a bunch of Guards from the front line to track you down — it's unprecedented. Now they're patrolling the whole city and everyone's in a panic.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Oh, we just—
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Not yet, March.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Bronya said we could trust you completely.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You mean to say that you don't trust me completely?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Good! That's smart of you. But you needn't worry, Cocolia and I aren't even on speaking terms. It was her that ejected me from the Architects — I refuse to stand with her.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I don't believe you guys would do anything bad, and the Architects are gonna need conclusive and publicly available evidence for me to think otherwise. Besides, I know the Architects, and if they did have any evidence, they would've released it by now.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I know Cocolia's style — get everyone into a frenzy first.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...Most people in a frenzy don't stop to ponder the details.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Ooh! I'm the best storyteller — let me! Let me!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Do you know Cocolia well?
Ooh! I'm the best storyteller — let me! Let me!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: So what details have you been pondering?
Telling Serval about your time in the Underworld and what you know about the Stellaron, and showing her Bronya's letter...
Do you dislike Cocolia?
Hehe, you could say that... We were like sisters once — inseparable. Of course, that was all before she became the supreme guardian...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Me? None. What Cocolia and the Architects get up to has nothing to do with me. My time is too precious for pondering.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Dislike? We were like sisters once — inseparable. Of course, that was all before she became the supreme guardian...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: These days I just spend my time fixing things in this workshop and playing music. It's a pretty carefree existence.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: *sigh* If I'm not careful I'll start boring you all with sob stories from the past. Let's get back to you guys. If long-lost Bronya told you to come here, you must have something important to tell me?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: You can trust me. I know our paths have only crossed once before, but my intuition tells me you guys are good people. And I've got good intuition by the way, haha.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...Try not to embellish the facts.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Perhaps I should do it, or we'll still be here tomorrow.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: So that's what's been happening — no wonder we hadn't heard from Bronya recently. *sigh* After all these years in isolation and without a single word from below, this is what's become of the Underworld...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I believe you, there's no way you could have invented all those twists and turns. What's more, we have Miss Seele here as living proof. As for the Stellaron... heh, I know why Bronya got you to find me.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...When I was still one of the Architects working in the Scientific Research Division, I was researching the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I never thought I'd hear that word again after being expelled by the Architects... Come on, I'll tell you everything.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Only a very few people in Belobog know of the existence of the Stellaron. Those that do would never associate it with the Fragmentum or Eternal Freeze.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: But according to the data recorded in that robot, Svarog... the Architects dug out the truth long ago. The research results were purposely hidden away to ensure that the outside world would never know of them.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Just my luck... Out of all the research topics I could've chosen, I insisted on the Stellaron. It's clear now that anyone who wanted to get closer to the truth would have been expelled or "abandoned."
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Maybe I should be thanking Cocolia. All she did was push me out... She could've decided to take a more permanent measure.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: How much do you know about the Stellaron?
Do you know what Cocolia's end goal is?
Can we talk to Gepard?
Do you know where the Stellaron is?

I figured out that the Stellaron and the Fragmentum were linked, so I was already close to the truth. It's a shame that the Architects ejected me before I could discover that the source of the Fragmentum was the Stellaron itself.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Before I lost my position, I was applying for permission to survey the Stellaron directly. It was my research topic, but I'd never even set eyes on it. My research was all based on historical data and lab simulations.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Not long after I submitted my preliminary report and application, I received my punishment. It was obvious that somebody didn't want my research to continue.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Cocolia... It's been so many years since we last spoke. We were great friends once — there was nothing we wouldn't share.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: She became a completely different person when she took on the supreme guardianship. The convictions she once held, her enthusiasm... it was like they were drawn out of her by some mysterious force.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: She gave the order to expel me herself and refused to see me... I never understood that behavior, and I gave up trying to use logic to work it out a long time ago.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Sometimes I even wonder whether she really did become a different person... is that possible? Perhaps there's a single guardian's consciousness that gets handed down from generation to generation... and the real Cocolia has already vanished.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Is she being compelled by previous generations of guardians to make such baffling decisions? Who knows... but this might make for good songwriting material.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Gepard? Not a chance... He's a decent guy, but also famously uncompromising.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: For my brother, orders are more important than anything. Even if you stuck Bronya's letter to his forehead, he wouldn't be swayed.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: You need to choose your words carefully if you want to persuade him of something. It might be best if I talk to him... though I'd need a strategy first.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Yes. I never observed it directly, but I used lab simulations and outbound surveys to establish a rough location.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: According to the survey results, the Stellaron is likely to the north of Belobog... somewhere in the vast Snow Plains.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: We must locate it as soon as possible — ideally before Cocolia takes action. Can you tell us the way?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Not a problem, I was thinking the same thing! But I'm afraid telling you might not be enough.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: The area to the north of Belobog has been more or less swallowed up by the Fragmentum. If you want to get to the northern Snow Plains, you'll need to get past the Silvermane Guard Restricted Zone on the front lines first.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Even if you get past the restricted zone in one piece... you'll have a whole heap of Fragmentum to deal with.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Silvermane Guard Restricted Zone?
A whole heap of Fragmentum...
Yes. That's where the main force of the Silvermane Guards is stationed. They've consolidated their position there in order to resist the encroaching Fragmentum.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Correct. And it's different from the underground towns you described. The Fragmentum there has quite literally torn everything to pieces — there's no sign of life, despite the monsters.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: It sounds like... The three of us and Seele might not be enough. Why don't we go back underground and get Wildfire to come with us?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I fear we may not have the time.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hey, enough pessimism! Back in my "official capacity" days, I spent a lot of time in the north — I got to know the soldiers and officers on the front line very well.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: This calls for brainwaves, not "brawnwaves." How about I take you over myself?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Really? Great! Phew, it's less scary if someone you know is leading the way!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Haha, I wanna see the Stellaron too, y'know — it was my research topic for over a decade. You don't get that many decades in life.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: That's settled then! There's no time to lose — we should head out as soon as you're ready.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: D—Darn it! I forgot my brother said he'd be around today...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Find somewhere to hide — quick — I'll handle him!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: G—Gepard, it's you! I didn't think you'd have the time to visit with things so tense on the front line, hehe...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Things are manageable, the latest wave of monster attacks has slowed. I'm back in the city to take care of a few matters, but I'll be back on the front line later... I thought I told you?
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Ah? Oh, yes, that's right...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...Sis, you look a bit pale. Did something happen?
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: N—No, why would anything have happened?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: You don't normally use my full name.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: *sigh* You said you hate it when I call you "bro" in public! Well I agree. It'd sound better if I started using your full name. Right, broseph?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...You can call me whatever you like. Look Serval, I'm here on official business today. There's something wrong with the Barrier Generator Device and the engineers in our unit don't know how to fix it. I need you to take a look.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Those guys can't think outside the box. Of course they can't wrap their heads around my design. *sigh* I thought it was something big. Leave it here. I'll take a look.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Hey! Who goes there?
rows.speaker: Patrolling Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Darn, he's spotted us!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Well, now we have to help him keep his mouth shut.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Halt, routine inspection!
rows.speaker: Patrolling Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Tsk, don't stand in our way!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Intruders! I must inform the security captain...
rows.speaker: Patrolling Silvermane Guard

rows.text: He's gonna raise the alarm, stop him!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Sorry to trouble you.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Why are you being so polite? Oh, and why's the city under curfew all of a sudden? Has something happened?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I... I've been instructed to keep it quiet.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Lil' Geppie... So grown up now... Looking down on his civilian sister...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Don't say that... *sigh* Forget it. If I don't tell you, Pela will...
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Last night, Lady Bronya suddenly appeared. She entered Qlipoth Fort without saying anything to anyone.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: The Supreme Guardian is worried that the three intruders may have followed Bronya out of the Fragmentum and back into the Administrative District. She issued a curfew for the entire city, and ordered us to pursue and capture any suspicious individuals.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Ah! So that's how it is, no wonder I haven't heard from Bronya... Is she alright?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I'm not sure. She hasn't left Qlipoth Fort. The supreme guardian just said she'd returned. Nothing more.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Well, I was sure worried about her... After she disappeared, Pela's workload doubled — she said she barely had time to go out.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: She really does tell you everything... Oh, by the way, I left my Goethe Hotel limited-edition flask behind last time I was here. Let me have a look for it. I think I left it over...
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: W—Wait!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: What is it? You seem pretty off today, Serval...
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: It's, um... right! You remember how you neglected all those flowers to death? I piled them all over there during a bit of spring cleaning, and now they smell terrible! So... don't go over there!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...Seems like a strange reason not to take a look... plus, am I supposed to believe you were spring cleaning? You must be up to more forbidden research...
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Am not — how dare you! What do you take your sister for?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: *sigh* Never mind. This is your space, and I shouldn't intrude. I've got business to take care of. Bye for now.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Hey! Wait a sec — uh... Those intruders, I wanted to ask. What crime have they committed?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: They're plotting to overthrow the Architects and bring harm to the city.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Huh... reminds me of the accusations against me. Cocolia's methods haven't changed.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Don't say that, Serval. I know that you're still nursing a grievance against the supreme guardian, but this isn't a joking matter.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: ...You're telling me off again. Fine, whatever bro. You better be going, come listen to Pela and my next rehearsal.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I will... if I have the time.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: The coast is clear. You can come out now.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Phew...I nearly suffocated! What kind of plot device was that...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I almost lost my cool when he went for his flask...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...This is bad. Bronya's in danger. We have to go save her.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Attempting to storm Qlipoth Fort by ourselves? Forget it, Seele. I don't care how skilled you are. I'm not sending you on a suicide mission.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Rest assured, Cocolia may have changed over the years... but she'd never hurt Bronya. I'm certain of that.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...You sound like Bronya herself. I don't get it — you guys are against Cocolia, and yet in some ways, you seem to trust her completely.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Have you thought of a way to persuade Gepard?
Is Gepard going to the Silvermane Guard Restricted Zone?
I was gauging his reactions just now, did you see? Unless we have irrefutable evidence, he won't question Cocolia's orders. If you go after him now, our plan's as good as over.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Didn't you hear him? He said he needs to take care of a few matters in the city first. If we're fast enough, we can stay out of his way.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Come on, let's go to the restricted zone. If we can get ahead of the curve and find the Stellaron, Cocolia will be out of options.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Is Bronya really safe?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: You care about her, huh. You must have become close friends.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Close is... a bit much. But I made her a promise...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Relax, she's the strongest girl I've ever seen.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Mm... I can believe that.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: They've jacked up security alright... how the heck are we gonna sneak in? Serval, we need one of those brainwaves.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Leave it to me. Stick close guys, and don't get spotted.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: This is a military base. Trespassers aren't allowed in.
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Wait, isn't that... Ah! Serval! Long time no see!
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Well, if it isn't Franz, long time no see! You're still watching the entrance?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Well you see, I... Bah, you haven't changed Serval. Still nailing us to the wall...
rows.speaker: Franz

rows.text: So... what brings you over here at this hour? And who are the guys behind you?
rows.speaker: Franz

rows.text: My brother said the restricted zone energy lines were malfunctioning — told me it was urgent. He doesn't trust those contracted maintenance workers... so he got me in for free.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: These guys are my assistants. We need to overhaul all the installations here.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Uh... I didn't hear anything about the energy lines malfunctioning...
rows.speaker: Franz

rows.text: Oh please, this is a Technology Division issue. Why would they tell you guys? Come on, let us in already. If the heating system goes down in the middle of the night, are you gonna be responsible for all the frozen corpses?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: N—No, that's uh, not something I could handle...
rows.speaker: Franz

rows.text: Seeing as you're Captain Gepard's sister, it should be fine...
rows.speaker: Franz

rows.text: Okay, here are some temporary passes... Oh, and remember to give them back to me when you leave.
rows.speaker: Franz

rows.text: Thanks, Franz. I'll put in a good word for you with my brother and get him to promote you!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: No, no, Captain Gepard hates all that under-the-table stuff. I'd have a better chance if you don't mention me at all...
rows.speaker: Franz

rows.text: I'm aware that there are those among you who see the reserve units as a vacation. Well let me set one thing straight: You are gravely mistaken!
rows.speaker: Guard Captain

rows.text: This is the restricted zone. The Fragmentum before you conceals monsters that watch your every move. Behind us, we have a band of conspirators that have infiltrated the city...
rows.speaker: Guard Captain

rows.text: The situation is critical... The lazy and undisciplined among you will lose your lives to the forces surrounding us!
rows.speaker: Guard Captain

rows.text: As such, starting from today, we will be adding 200 bench presses and 30 extra minutes of one-arm planks to our daily drill! Is that clear?
rows.speaker: Guard Captain

rows.text: Well said, Serval!
Think thrice, Gepard!
What happened to brainwaves!?
We don't need you to yield.
Please yield already.
Brainwaves? Anyone?
Final answer...?
We could decide for you.
Fine! I've still got fight in me.
Thanks for understanding.
Is this a brainwave? This feels like a brainwave.
Nice interpretation of the rules, dude.
Yes, sir!
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: See! That was easy.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: You're Gepard's sister alright...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmph, I don't want people to see me that way... I'm doing this for you. Otherwise, I wouldn't be using my brother's name.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Hmm... Are those... temporary passes?
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: I haven't seen one of those for a long time. Hmm... The restricted zone virtually never allows outsiders in.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Do you see that mechanical gear bridge? When you cross over to the other side, you arrive at hell on earth.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: So what exactly is on the other side?
And what's this "hell" like exactly?
The Architects follow Qlipoth. Do they believe in hell?
An endless Fragmentum, a few exhausted Silvermane Guards... and the stench of death in the air.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Hm... It's a place too cold to bear, covered in snow and ice. The guys doing the scientific research don't have time to worry about the surroundings.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: The restricted zone front line is on the other side of the gear bridge. It's an endless Fragmentum with a few exhausted Silvermane Guards... and the stench of death in the air.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: They do. The Architects believe that hell can exist on any world — a plight that will inevitably come to be without intervention.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: In the future, a terrible catastrophe will arrive. If, under Qlipoth the Preservation's guidance, we fail to construct a barrier, that catastrophe will sweep away the stars, plunging all worlds into hell.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: That's the belief of the Architects... but for us, hell is an endless Fragmentum, a few exhausted Silvermane Guards... and the stench of death in the air.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: If we want to progress further north, we will need to cross that hell. Are you ready?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: We've come this far...
Without hardships to overcome, there is no trailblazing.
It's never too late to retreat...
Exactly, we've got nowhere left to retreat.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Right on! I'm stealing that!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Look how far we've come! Don't chicken out on us now.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Haha, let's go then. First, we need to think of a way to get to the other side.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I helped set the underlying mechanisms for this type of gear bridge. It's controlled via different terminals in combination. Let's go find them.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Is Gepard on front line duty a lot?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yes, but what made you ask that all of a sudden?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: It's so dangerous, don't you worry about him?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He's a Landau.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...Mechanical Fever released a new song. Did you hear it?
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Sure did, Pela was on lead vocals this time, scared me half to death. It's a completely different style.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Even Mechanical Fever is changing... *sigh* Rock 'n' roll's dead, there's no audience anymore.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Don't be so pessimistic. They're just keeping things fresh. I thought Pela was pretty good.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Argh...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Nope... this terminal is offline, we can't control it from here.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: So what's the plan?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Look for another — every platform linked to the gear bridge should have a similar terminal.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I never would've guessed that Gepard and you were brother and sister.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I can't say I blame you — we're nothing alike in personality or interests.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: In our family we have a strong military tradition going back generations — many a Landau has died in their prime. There's not a lot of "brother and sister time." Everyone just does their best to get on with their life.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...Darn, can't activate it. It seems like someone's severed the energy supply to the terminals.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: So someone's deliberately trying to create trouble?
Are the Guards doing this intentionally?
Did we do this?
I... huh. Y'know, the more I think about it, the more it seems deliberate.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I was just thinking that, we can't rule it out.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: What are you talking about...?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I think the Guards must have done this intentionally.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: With the front line on high alert, they must have rotated the bridge to make it impassable. Then they cut off the energy supply to the terminals to avoid accidental repositioning... or to prevent deserters from escaping.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: That way, even if the front line were to collapse... the Fragmentum monsters wouldn't be able to make it to the other side.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: They cut off their only retreat...
That's terrible.
Wise tactics.
Bronya was right... The Silvermane Guards really are risking their lives to protect Belobog.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Just my conjecture, but I doubt it's far from the truth. My brother mentioned that they've had to use extreme measures to repel the Fragmentum monsters.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Let's press on. We can't activate either of these terminals, so let's look for the energy supply installation itself.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Aren't you the maintenance people? What are you doing over here?
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: You can't just go wherever you please in the restricted zone! Get to work!
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Sorry, I'm on duty, no time to chat.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: If there's an issue, report to the security captain.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: That's it! The thing shaped like a giant iron ball.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: And it's behind a gate. What are the odds...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Its formal name is the "mechanism energy hub." It's connected to all the energy lines — I would've thought it covers the entire restricted zone.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Mm... no wonder it's so heavily guarded.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: One unit for everything? That's a disaster waiting to happen — we learned the hard way.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: As long as we can gain access permissions to the hub, we can operate the gear bridge terminals.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Won't this cause a commotion...?
Won't the Guards get suspicious?
That's why I told them we were here for urgent maintenance! The front line equipment needs servicing just as much as the rest.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: So that's why you went for maintenance, way to go Serval! I thought you just came up with it on the spot.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Come on, let's see if that guard over there will let us past.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Yo! Evening, soldier!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Are you the emergency engineers? I saw you guys hanging around. Did you find the problem?
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Not yet, everything looks normal so far. I think the problem is stemming from the energy hub.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: If you let us in we can do a routine service inspection... I've worked on various iterations of this type of installation...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Haha, no, no, no, no... No can do! No one gets near the energy hub without the security captain's encryption key.
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Uh, not even the supreme guardian?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The supreme guardian...? Hey, no games, y'hear? No dice without the encryption key!
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Darn, this guy's not stupid...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You need the encryption key, right? Which captain should I bother then?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...Captain Dunn's resting up ahead. Go and find him. If he grants you permission, I won't stand in your way.
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Dunn... Dunn? Ha, why didn't you say so! No problem. We'll be back in a bit.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Serval, this Dunn, do you know him?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You bet I do. We go way back. He's easy to talk to. Watch me persuade him.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Hmm-hmm... Did you hear Mallick is being reassigned? It seems like both the front line and the city are shorthanded right now.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Seriously? No way. I thought Mallick had only just been promoted?
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Mysterious. It feels like something big's about to go down.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: As long as it's away from the front line, I'd happily be reassigned... It's only been a year since I enlisted — I'm not ready to lose my life.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Ahh, you make it sound terrible. Good luck "preserving" anything with those idlers in the reserve units. Our purpose as Silvermane Guards is to protect the citizens of Belobog.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: You, hold it right there!
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: This is a military base. Temporary workers aren't allowed in.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: I heard Gepard sent mechanics for an emergency repair?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: Yes, I confirmed it with Franz.
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard

rows.text: I've been keeping watch here all day, why didn't I hear about any equipment in need of emergency servicing?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: I heard from Franz that it's Captain Gepard's sister...
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard

rows.text: S—Serval!?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: ...You gotta be kidding me, I haven't showered in two days... do I smell?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: ...N—No, sir!
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Hey, Dunn! It's been a while. I didn't know you made security captain.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: S—Serval, it's been a long time... you're still so... Ahem. You look good.
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: Allow me to introduce my assistants to you. They help me take care of business at the workshop.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Everyone, this is Captain Dunn, an old friend of mine. He used to be an ace on the keys in the band.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Oh? You play rock 'n' roll too? Cool!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Pleased to meet you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Great seeing you.
Something smells weird...
Oh, hello...
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: *sniff* What's that weird smell...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmm? *cough* Zackery, how many days has it been since you showered?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: Uh... I showered right before my shift—
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Hmm? What did you say?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: ...I—I haven't showered in two days, sir!
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Unacceptable, especially in front of visitors! Apologies for the embarrassment, all.
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: It's not a big deal, Dunn. Y'know, if you get a chance, would you wanna get on stage with us again?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: My keyboard guy is pretty good, but I still miss our military days playing in the band...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: That was a long time ago, Serval — I haven't touched a keyboard in ages. Besides, I'm stationed here all year round, I'm afraid I don't get many chances to return to the city.
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: Though I don't stand on ceremony... How may I assist you? If everything's in order, you'd better head back to the city. It's not safe here.
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: I've checked the lines, there don't seem to be any major problems. All that's left is the energy hub.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: The guard over there said that I needed an "encryption key" to open the gate. Can you help me out?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: We'll be on our way after we run a check-up.
Don't be hesitant in front of your dream girl.
Could you be any less discreet!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Anything wrong, Dunn?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Sorry, Serval... but can you tell me what Captain Gepard told you?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: Huh? Oh, uh... Let me think... "Hey sis, the energy supply lines in the restricted zone have malfunctioned. Those useless engineers can't find the problem." Something like that...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: And may I ask... when did he contact you?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: Uh... this morning? Yeah, that's right. He's on urban patrol duty today, right? That's why he popped round and asked the favor.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I heard that there's an arrest warrant out in the city for some major criminals — they even recalled some of the Guards.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: It never ends. Things are bad enough on the front line without things going south behind us...
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: At least Captain Gepard's here, they say he captured the fugitives once already.
rows.speaker: Guard

rows.text: Captain Gepard just returned to the front line. I could... reconfirm with him?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: ...Hah? Hold up, he's back? That can't be, he was still in the city a little while ago...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: *sigh* You haven't changed Serval... You're still a lousy liar.
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: These people you've brought, they're... they're not workshop assistants, right?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: Serval, it's not that I don't want to help you... but you should remember that I'm a Belobog Silvermane Guard!
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: How about this. You can leave and I won't tell anyone about this incident... But the outsiders must remain.
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: There goes the negotiation.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Serval, you should go.
Sorry for getting you involved in this.
Looks like this is gonna end in a fight after all...
I brought you guys here, and I'm standing with you till the end!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Dunn, this concerns the fate of Belobog — no — the fate of our whole world. Please don't stand in our way...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Serval! We used to rehearse together every day. You must understand?
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: My rock 'n' roll soul is to uphold the dignity of a soldier!
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: Serval... why...
rows.speaker: Dunn

rows.text: I'm sorry Dunn... Time for a little nap.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: He's just unconscious. Don't worry.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Stubborn fool... strong, though. Wildfire lacks people like him.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Got it, the encryption key! Quick, before we attract attention, let's—
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I think we attracted attention...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's the enemy attack alarm... Every Silvermane Guard in the reserve zone just became our enemy.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Come on, let's take them out!
If we work together we can break through their ranks!
My life was short, but it was a life filled with—
You're not dead yet. How can you give up that easily!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We've made it up till now... I could lose an arm and a leg for all I care — I have to lay eyes on the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Quick, back to the energy supply hub. Anyone that tries to stop us is gonna find out a thing or two.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: If I'd known he had the encryption key from the start, I could've snuck in and taken it off him myself.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Shoulda, coulda, woulda, Seele! Activating the gear bridge alone would've been enough to expose us.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: We're in!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: It's open! Oh, thank you, thank you, thank you, Dunn!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Give me some time...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Ugh, who designed this operating system! It's so unintuitive!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Come on, let's take them out!
If we work together we can break through their ranks!
My life was short, but it was a life filled with—
Emergency Fire Evacuation System... Not that...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Rock 'n' Roll Dance Floor Atmosphere Mode... Who the heck added that!? And they used one of my songs!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Gear Bridge Control Terminal — ha, still found it!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: That's it, I've reset the energy system! Let's go and operate the gear bridge terminal.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Um, Serval... won't more Silvermane Guards be waiting for us on the other side of the gear bridge?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yup.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Then what's our plan!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Well, either we reason with them or charge straight through the blockade... Let's play it by ear!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Uhh...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Careful! There's a big guy up ahead.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: There's no other way... We'll have to fight.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Hmph, if we can beat Svarog, we can beat this one. Let's go!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Energy restored... system online... certification enabled... come on, come on!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Phew! We did it! We've gained access to the gear bridge. Let's move.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Perfect! Okay, we need to get to the front line.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...We could have a problem. Your brother may be there.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: He probably is... Hopefully, we don't bump into him, but if we do, we'll just have to try and talk to him...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Are you sure you can convince him?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I've probably got a 30% chance, or less.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...Meaning it could end in a fight.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Haven't you noticed yet? Most of our "convincing" ends in a fight.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We need to be sure, Serval. If we can't reach a common understanding with your brother... will you stand with us?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Of course. My word is my bond. I said that I'd stand with you to the end, and I won't go back on that promise.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Before our next expedition, I need Himeko to teach me some negotiation skills. Beating people up all the time is cramping my elegance!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I haven't fought with Gepard since he enlisted. He could never beat me when we were little, but now...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Serval... it really is you.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Wait, Gepard! Listen to me—
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: When the sentry reported to me, I thought there must have been a misunderstanding. The enemy alarm had to be unrelated to your entry into the restricted zone — perhaps the intruders had taken you hostage. And yet...
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Step away from the intruders, Serval. Walk over slowly and stand behind me. You're different from them.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: I'm sorry... we have an understanding. I stand with them.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Give me a few minutes, just a few. I'll explain every—
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Enough, Serval!
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Have you forgotten where we are? We Landaus ought to know this place better than anywhere... The outer reaches of the front line against the Fragmentum, Belobog's most strategic protective fortress.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Every Silvermane Guard here, every person here, is ready to sacrifice themselves, ready to spill their blood for Belobog at a moment's notice...
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Yet here you are leading fugitives into the restricted zone, attacking my Silvermane comrades-in-arms, hijacking the energy hub... Are you really worthy of the Landau name?
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Why do you think I've come here? We've found a way to dispel the Eternal Freeze, to seal the Fragmentum. It might be the only lifeline this world has left!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: If that were true, why wouldn't you report to Madam Cocolia? Why would you sneak into the restricted zone and create chaos!?
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: You don't understand. The one preventing us from getting close to the truth... is Cocolia herself.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...You have all seen the supreme guardian in person. Do you think you can act as you please because she didn't recognize your version of events!?
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Listen to me, Gepard! The origin and spread of the Fragmentum is linked to the Stellaron. The meteorite in the Architects' records, it's—
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I know about the Stellaron. It's exactly what the fugitives behind you are seeking. But the Madam Guardian has already revealed the truth to me! These people have ulterior motives, Serval. They want to steal this treasure from the Architects.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: The Madam Guardian has warned me before that you were indulging in fantasy, that you'd been exposed to forbidden knowledge, and that you would bring destruction down upon Belobog... I believe you, Serval, I believe you think you're acting with loyalty to the people! It's just...
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Guards, formation! Arrest these people. We could be inundated with Fragmentum monsters at any moment, we have no time to waste on them!
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: The forbidden is only forbidden to conceal the truth within.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Cocolia's afraid that we'll seize on this knowledge — that the truth will spread far and wide: To save the world, we must risk it all.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I've said my piece, whether you believe it or not is up to you. Regardless, you should know by now your sister's never been one to back down. If there's something or someone you can't abide, you should stand up and resist... and if there's something you uphold, you should uphold it to the very end!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Well said, Serval!
Think thrice, Gepard!
What happened to brainwaves!?
Save your explanation for the judge. You are charged with sabotaging the Silvermane Guard Restricted Zone. In my capacity as captain, I hereby order that these fugitives be arrested!
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: This isn't like our childhood games, Serval. You won't get any leniency from me.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: The Barrier hasn't been fixed yet. Don't try and be a hero, Gepard!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...Ugh, didn't I tell you? All our negotiations end in combat!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This guy... knows how to put up a fight. I've never come up against anyone this relentless!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Phew... he just won't go down...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He's as stubborn as I am. It could be an argument or a fight — he'll do both to the death... That's why he bugs the heck out of me!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: That's enough, Gepard. Take a look around you! You're the last man standing!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...Even if I am, I won't yield...
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: We don't need you to yield.
Please yield already.
Brainwaves? Anyone?
We don't want you to yield through force of arms. That wouldn't be a victory for us.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yeah, our goal is the same as yours, Serval's, and Bronya's — we just want to preserve this world! There's no reason to turn against each other!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Gepard... brother. Surely now you can see the need for pragmatism?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Even if you don't believe my outsider friends, you should believe me... Ugh, maybe I've wasted your trust... in which case, believe Bronya.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...Lady Bronya?
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: You tell Gepard everything you know and show him Bronya's letter.
There's nothing more to say, Gepard. The decision is yours.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: As a captain of the Silvermane Guards, I am duty-bound to carry out the orders of the Supreme Guardian.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Final answer...?
We could decide for you.
Fine! I've still got fight in me.

But... Lady Bronya is the commanding officer for the front lines. According to military protocol, if the front line directives of the commanding officer clash with those of the Architects behind the lines, a soldier must remain at their post and await further directives.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Thanks for understanding.
Is this a brainwave? This feels like a brainwave.
Nice interpretation of the rules, dude.
For the Silvermane Guards, the guardian's orders are paramount and absolute. But there is something of equal importance in the oath we take...
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: ...The people of Belobog.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: If we lose the people, we lose the reason for our existence. Our fight with the Fragmentum monsters is for the sake of preservation, but our fight with you... I fail to see the purpose.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: If you are truly able to prevent our endlessly unfolding misfortunes, then the people of Belobog are indebted to you.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: But if you are using lies to mask your true intentions, using my sister and Bronya for your own ends... I swear by Qlipoth that I will carry out your punishment without an ounce of mercy.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: They're not lying, I promise you.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: You must be Seele? You are a skilled fighter... your combat style is nothing like that of the Guards.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Regardless of what you believe, these guys have been a great help to the Underworld. Many people would vouch for them.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...I'm sure.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: If you want to advance further northward, you must traverse an area entirely corroded by the Fragmentum. It's the only way to get to the Snow Plains on the other side.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: The Guards can give you some time before the next wave of attacks is upon us.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: I gotta admit, I had a lot of... misunderstandings... about the Silvermane Guards. They're fighting for survival here every day, just like Wildfire.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Sorry for getting you involved in this.
So this is how brothers and sisters normally coexist?
Let the Stellaron hunt begin.
We've got this.
The difference is we're making a stand for freedom... while they're just carrying out orders.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: That's why we have to try and put ourselves in their shoes.
Do you understand Bronya's struggles?
It's time to finish this.
Put ourselves in their shoes... Easier said than done. Everyone has their struggles, but how can we understand them if we can't even see each other?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Of course I do, I've understood them for a while now. But as far as I can tell, she doesn't need other people's understanding. She needs to understand her own heart.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...It's the same with Gepard. I could tell it took a lot for him to lay down his arms.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I think I can already hear the storm on the other side of the city walls... Not a reassuring sound.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I hope Serval's right... That supreme lunatic better not have harmed Bronya.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: You see? Brothers and sisters need to have a scrap once in a while to get back on good terms.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Agh, enough apologizing. My ears can't take any more.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Honestly, this would have happened sooner or later. You just gave me an excuse to bring everything forward.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: What's wrong with a bit of violent coexistence between siblings? Seems pretty normal to me.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Hehe, I'm pulling your leg. Since I left the military, my brother and I have always steered clear of certain sensitive topics... Thinking about it, perhaps he's just been looking out for my feelings, shielding me all along.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Knowing my temper, my brother almost certainly went to great lengths on many occasions for me. I should be thanking him.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Let's do this. I may never have come face to face with it, but this Stellaron cost me a nice, stable job. It's time to get even.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Actually, I have another selfish motive... I want to prove to Cocolia that I was right. Once we've taken care of the Stellaron... maybe she'll go back to how she was.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...Sorry, hardly the time for me to be obsessing over all this.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: As I mentioned, if we want to progress further north, we're gonna have to cross that "hell." Still, look at it this way: Just another arena to showcase our skills, right?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Now, if you're ready to get on stage, let's push for that standing ovation!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Come on, let's take them out!
If we work together we can break through their ranks!
My life was short, but it was a life filled with—
Well said, Serval!
Think thrice, Gepard!
What happened to brainwaves!?
We don't need you to yield.
Please yield already.
Brainwaves? Anyone?
Final answer...?
We could decide for you.
Fine! I've still got fight in me.
Thanks for understanding.
Is this a brainwave? This feels like a brainwave.
Nice interpretation of the rules, dude.
As soon as the restricted zone gate is open, the monsters on the other side will turn out in full force. The Guards will do their best to stall them and buy you some time.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Once you've broken through the front line... there's nothing more we can do for you. You'll have to find out for yourselves what lies within the northern Fragmentum.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: So... have you made up your minds?
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: We're ready.
Give us a moment...
Understood. Keep your weapons close. This will be a fierce fight.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Guards! Open the gate!
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Are you dealing with attacks like this every day?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: It's a common occurrence.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Guards, formation!
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Hmph, well I'm gonna make sure I don't owe the Guards any favors when this is done!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: For Bronya!
For Belobog!
For universal peace!
Here they come!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Steel yourselves!
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Argh...
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: ...I told you, Gepard, the Barrier hasn't been fixed yet! Don't try and be a hero!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: This is... only the first wave. They'll have reassembled soon... I have to...
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Hey, Mr. Silvermane, listen to your sister! I can tell just by looking at you that you haven't fully recovered.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Outsiders, Seele, the second wave hasn't started yet. Make the most of this opportunity and make a break for it!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Huh? Serval, aren't you gonna look for the Stellaron with us?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: My brother can't hold them back by himself. He wasted a lot of energy on us. He's my responsibility now. Besides...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: If I'm not here to help... I don't know what might happen in the next wave.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I want to go with you, I do! I always wanted to catch a glimpse of the Stellaron with my own eyes, and now it's so close...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: But I can't abandon my brother and the other Guards — I'm a Landau! It's up to you now, I believe in you. You've given me new hope!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Get hold of the Stellaron before Cocolia realizes what's happening!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: We can't abandon you either!
We won't disappoint you.
Chaaaaarge!
Serval's right, [Trailblazer]. Let's go.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: The Guards have opened up a way through for us, we can't let them down.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hey March! Don't forget to take a picture of the Stellaron for me.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Say no more! We're good at this. Don't worry!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Fragmentum activity is intensifying... Something's happening on Jarilo-VI.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Shouldn't we go down there, Himeko?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Have faith in them. Besides, this is {M#his}{F#her} first Trailblazing expedition. How will {M#he}{F#she} be able to look back fondly without a few twists and turns?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Are you bored, Welt? I understand... But we have lots of opportunities ahead of us. Let's leave the memories of this expedition for them~
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: So you think they'll be safe, right?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...Yes, we haven't seen any Aeon or Emanator-level imaginary reactions. Relax.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: This is a young person's adventure, we shouldn't interfere. At most, we could offer a little "off-site assistance."
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Is this... the Fragmentum Gepard was talking about?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Compared to this, the corrosion we saw in Backwater Pass pales into insignificance.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...This place makes my flesh crawl... like there are insects under my skin.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: We have no guide and no way of detecting the Stellaron. We'll just have to advance gradually... and cautiously.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Don't be disheartened. The stronger the Fragmentum contamination, the closer we are to the source.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Look, up ahead on the ground... What is that?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Be careful, think twice before you interact with anything in the Fragmentum.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Objects that have been exposed to Fragmentum corrosion might not be stable. I wouldn't touch that device if I were you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: We're deep inside the Fragmentum... There could be hidden dangers lying in wait.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's look for other clues first.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This is... Bronya's!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: We found it in the orphanage...
Could she be here too?
Yeah! So she's... she's been here already?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Right, she must be! This can't be a coincidence.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: This is the spirit of trailblazing!
Wh—Whoa! Quick, look!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's Bronya! H—Huh? Is that Cocolia too!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: How can we pinpoint the Stellaron?
There's a restless atmosphere here.
Oh yeah, [Trailblazer]. It feels like... like there are loads of eyes staring at us.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Serval said that the Stellaron was very likely hidden in the Snow Plains north of Belobog. If we want to get there, I'm afraid we'll have to find the exit to this Fragmentum maze first.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Serval said that the Stellaron was very likely hidden in the Snow Plains north of Belobog. If we want to get there, I'm afraid we'll have to find the exit to this Fragmentum maze first.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Guys... does this place feel weird to you? It feels like... like there are loads of eyes staring at us.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: No, it isn't them.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It must be... a kind of echo? Some type of residual energy replicated by the Fragmentum...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Which means they were definitely here, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: And it looks like they went that way.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ha, just in time! We had no idea which direction to take. Let's go!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...You still haven't told me what this place is, mother.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Seven hundred years ago, this was Belobog's northern border and the site of an ancient battle. Here is where Alisa Rand led the first Silvermane Guards in resistance against the Legion.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Now... it is nothing more than an abandoned corridor, filled with the sounds of Old World echoes.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Don't let its fragmented appearance fool you, Bronya. On the day the promise is fulfilled... these ruins will become the breeding ground of a new world.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: ...Mother, do you truly believe the Stellaron's promise? It summoned the blizzard beyond our walls and opened the door of the Fragmentum. It destroyed our civilization, it...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...And yet, the crime of our ancestors was their inability to embrace that destruction sooner...
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: From the moment those intruders descended from beyond the sky, this world was handed a death sentence. But the Stellaron... has reserved for us a thread of hope.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: There is a price to pay for new life. Wiping away every decaying vestige of the Old World, renouncing the meaningless and lingering struggle... This is the price the Stellaron demands.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: When the promise is fulfilled, Bronya... no longer will we have to squander our lives guarding this wasteland. You and I will witness the new world rise from the ruins.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: This is a complex mechanism. How did they get past?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: *sigh* I knew this wouldn't be simple...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wait! Wasn't there some big energy hub-looking thing back in that empty area? Let's go back and take a look, maybe it's linked to this gate.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I can't say I like the idea of interacting with our surroundings — especially this deep into the Fragmentum. However...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: However?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...There's no other way. Desperate times call for desperate measures.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Ha, even Dan Heng the sensible has his adventurous days!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It worked, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...But, the gate didn't move an inch...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* Are there other units around?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Hmm. It's clear that whoever designed these mechanisms didn't want outsiders to get through too easily. Let's keep looking for the energy hub.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Look over there! I think I can see the next unit.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...I see it too — let's go.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Are those monsters guarding the energy hub?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It seems like it... Strange. Fragmentum monsters would usually destroy man-made objects.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Did you hear that? This mechanism must be on now!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Come on, let's find the next one!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Where is the next mechanism... Oh, behind that gate.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: There's no switch. We need to find a way around.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I've never seen such a desolate place... At least in Rivet Town, you could tell that people used to live there.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Rivet Town is only at the outstretched fingertips of the corrosion... Now, we're deep in the Fragmentum's heart.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Success! Another mechanism shut down.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer], I want to ask you a question.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Ask away.
Is now a good time?
Yes, I think this could well be the best time.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Do you still remember those dreams you mentioned to us?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I know you're wide awake right now, but I need you to try. See if you can recall the "voice" you heard.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Danger... approaches...
rows.speaker: Voice of the Stellaron

rows.text: You must...eradicate... Once... and for all...
rows.speaker: Voice of the Stellaron

rows.text: Well?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There was... a voice calling out to Cocolia...
The voice... it knows we're getting close.
(Try to repeat the whispers you heard)
This is merely speculation... but perhaps the voice you heard is the Stellaron somehow conveying information to Cocolia...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...and the one in your body... is resonating with the Stellaron on this world.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Huh!? You mean that Stellarons can communicate? I've never heard that before...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Well, there's never been a human that could accommodate a Stellaron in their body.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The Stellaron knows we're here...
The Stellaron has already warned Cocolia...
...Then, aren't we walking straight into a trap?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Yes. And Bronya may well be the bait.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Dan Heng's speculations are usually right on the money. But even if we've guessed right, we can't go home now.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmph... there's no way back anyway. At least Cocolia won't catch us off guard now. So what if it's an ambush!? We're not about to lose now!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I have to save Bronya, beat Cocolia, and crush this Stellaron thing to dust!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Uh... Is this right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: If we want to get to the other side, we'll need to rotate the gear bridge again and go around.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Done! It took some effort, but we finally cracked these mechanisms...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We're one step closer to Bronya. Let's move!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: *gasp* Are these echoes too?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yes. The Fragmentum here seems to have made a special connection with Cocolia. It's repeatedly generating forms in her image.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I don't understand... Even if the truth is as you say, every generation of guardian has resisted the call of the Stellaron...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: (Close eyes and meditate)
(Give it a halfhearted attempt)
You try to recall the dreams. As your train of thought deepens, the voice comes to you...
You close your eyes but don't expect to remember anything. And yet, the voice comes to you...
Can all of them have been wrong, mother?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Do you still not see, Bronya? There is no right or wrong here. Some of them acted out of human pride, others out of human shortsightedness.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Our ancestors... including Alisa Rand... spent their whole lives trying to prolong this civilization. Then, after all fell still, their memories were scattered by the blizzard.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: They spent lifetimes writing songs of praise that lauded the bravery of humanity, but couldn't spare the time to gaze up into the stars.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: To those entities of greater magnificence in the heavens above, a thousand years is but a passing moment, the attainments of insignificant beings nothing more than a footnote.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: I shall not follow the guardians' misguided steps down that blind alley of narcissism. If persistence is futile, then one must choose a new beginning.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: But, Qlipoth the Preservation... Are THEY not one of the magnificent entities you speak of? Is it not THEIR strength... that has sheltered Belobog this entire time?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The Preservation... Has the Preservation ever looked humanity in the eye? Nothing more than an arrogant delusion of the Architects.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: You will hear the real voice of magnificence, Bronya... Then, you will understand my choice.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Whoa, check this place out! Tables and sentry posts — there must have been Silvermane Guards stationed here once.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: If there were, they left a long time ago. There might be valuable information here... shame we don't have time to look for it.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Looks like another completely new monster.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Considering where we are, it would be surprising if we didn't run into strange enemies here.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I don't care how strange it is, it's blocking our way... Let's get it!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: This enemy is completely different! If I didn't know it was a product of the Fragmentum, I'd think we were fighting a human!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Unlike those random low-level Fragmentum creations, this one seems to have a mind of its own. It seems to be able to use complex tactics.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Look, Bronya and Cocolia's echoes... they must have come through here.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The voice is getting clearer...
I'm starting to feel hazy...
...That means we must be really close, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey, stay with it! This is the final push!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I sense that we're very near to the northern Snow Plains.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: This is where the first guardian led the Silvermane Guards into battle. She made huge sacrifices for the sake of temporary respite.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: But the otherworldly Legion did not tire. She soon realized that flesh and blood could not contend with so ruthless an enemy.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: When all was nearly lost, she chose to set her sights on the Stellaron... and made the first wish.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: As for what came later... you know as well as I.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: So... the Eternal Freeze was a disaster brought about by a human wish...?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Ironic, no? All the Stellaron did was answer humanity's call, and yet we kept its existence a closely guarded secret for centuries.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Even going so far as to attempt to use "it" to control the Stellaron... Woeful... laughable.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: It?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Something created using otherworldly technology... An inhibitor that a corporation from the Old World and the Architects attempted to use to house the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: ...I know you have many questions, my daughter. Be patient... soon you will have all the answers.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: It's that "shadow" of hers again... but Bronya's isn't with her this time.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: It's only a Fragmentum illusion. [Trailblazer], let's get a closer look.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It feels like this echo is different from the others before.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Intruders...
rows.speaker: Cocolia's Echo

rows.text: Huh!? Did... Did she just speak!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You cannot... approach...
rows.speaker: Cocolia's Echo

rows.text: Not good — March, out the way!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...the Stellaron!
rows.speaker: Cocolia's Echo

rows.text: ...She disappeared.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Those stairs... it's the only way forward.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Wherever they lead, it must be the end of the journey.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: If we avoid the enemy, we might be ambushed further in.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It'll be too late for regrets then... Let's defeat this one here.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I don't wanna get to the end so soon... I want my journey to go on forever.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This means that Bronya is up ahead... and so is the fate of the Overworld and the Underworld... It's all in our hands.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Strange, I thought I'd feel nervous or afraid... but I don't. The only feeling I have... is that none of this seems real.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Is this how Trailblazing expeditions usually come to an end?
These two have gotten used to these expeditions.
Resting forever in the Snow Plains... that wouldn't be so bad.
Not always, sometimes it's a happier conclusion.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: To be honest, you never really get used to them! We always used to rely on Himeko and Mr. Yang.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey, way to boost morale over there!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The Express has traveled world after world. We are merely passing travellers — witnesses to part of a grander story.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: We invariably avoid getting drawn into turbulence that can decide the fate of a world... but there are always times when we have no choice but to act.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Or to put it another way, [Trailblazer]... this is one heck of a first Trailblazing expedition! You hit the jackpot!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I was about to bore you all with my gloomy reflections... but on second thought — not today. Adventuring with you guys by my side has made me feel like no obstacle is too big.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Right on! But you can say whatever you like — a good adventure shouldn't be full of rules and regulations!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Helping those in need, befriending those worth counting on, and saving the world a few times along the way...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hey, it's too dangerous to operate the mechanism with them here... We better clean this place up first!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: It's f—freezing here — the blizzard's so fierce! The power from the Trailblaze Path isn't enough to stop the cold...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It means that we're getting closer to the Stellaron... and the heart of the Eternal Freeze.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Wh—What is this? ...It's scary!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...It's like an insect trapped in amber...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I bet the Antimatter Legion forces never thought they'd be swallowed up by the Eternal Freeze when they invaded this world.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Even in the ice... could these guys still be alive...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wanna defrost them and find out?
Is this how you were...?
I hereby name him: March 8th.
No, no! We've got enough on our plate.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I... I don't remember... It's a blank canvas...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm impressed you can still think up jokes right now...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Did the Architects build this...?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: The frozen remains of Voidrangers are scattered along the mountain path. Even the ruthless Antimatter Legion is helpless against the might of the Eternal Freeze.
The Voidranger remains are preserved remarkably well in the ice. You can't help but wonder... perhaps March 7th is right.
—Either way, you think that it's best not to unfreeze them.
...The future of Belobog rests in my hands!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Behold, the end is upon you!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: I—It's bigger than I thought... Hey you, I was just joking! Leave us alone, shoo!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Incoming, look out!
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: This energy flow... it's up to something.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: There's something on its right hand, stay alert!
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Gotcha! See, that's what you get for annoying me!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: No, the Legion's weapon shouldn't go down so easily.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Let's worry about that later. We need to focus fire — fast.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Is everybody okay?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm out, I'm out! It's gone bananas!
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Not good... It's ready to throw everything at us.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Hey! Is it trying to pull a charged attack?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I don't see any other possibilities. Here we go, brace yourselves!
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...very different from the uniform style of the buildings we saw in the city.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Does it... look like the palm of a huge hand to you?
rows.speaker: March 7th
