rows.text: If Cocolia threatens us by taking Bronya hostage...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We have to save her. The Underworld... no, the entire planet relies on her.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Do not resist, Bronya... Accept the common will!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: No... I... I don't want this...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Look upon their promised future, Bronya! A world without poverty, without cold, without suffering... A world where people no longer have to pray like prisoners for survival... A world that we can guard for all eternity.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Seven hundred years ago, we tried and fought unceasingly, believing that the radiance of human nature could shepherd us towards rejuvenation. And to what end? A crushing defeat!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Why, when faced with irrefutable strength, is our first thought always to resist, to cover our ears, instead of hearing the call?
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: It is the conceit and cowardice entrenched in the depths of human nature — so difficult to efface. Cast them aside, break free of the chains that bind you! The Stellaron will lead humanity to evolve, and THEY will...
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Your brainwashing ends here, you witch!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Seele?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...You came. I thought the blizzards had entombed you...
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: You wish! We're not going down before you do!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Bronya! I don't know what happened between you and them. Even if you explained it to me, I probably wouldn't understand all the crazy details. But there are two things I do know...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: One: These guys have come through hell to get here — to seal this Stellaron thing.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: And two: Do you remember what I said? If anything happened to you, I'd save you.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Do you understand? Even if the damage is done — even if you've completely forgotten our promise, then... then I'm just gonna have to knock you out and bring you back myself!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Seele, all of you...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Finished? I think I've given you long enough, to... bid farewell.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: It's time I told you my other reason for bringing you here, Bronya.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: I want to witness your choice.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: I have told you all the truths there are to tell: The deal with the Stellaron, the wish I made to it... There are no more secrets between us.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Many years ago, the voice of the Stellaron sounded in my ears for the first time. I was no different from the previous generations of guardians... I withdrew, refused to hear. I was as you are now — bitterly defending the Architects' so-called "Preservation..."
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: My conviction was once steadfast, unparalleled... until a sudden change arrived and threw everything into chaos. Another choice appeared before me — a subversion of the old order... and the welcoming of a new world.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: And compared to the illusory, evermore distant Preservation, this was so tangible...
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: I have agonized — long agonized over how to convey all this to you. Inevitably, the promised tomorrow will transpire... but if you were not there beside me, to watch over that new world...
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: ...Then I would descend into torment, Bronya — enduring torment!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Perhaps I should be thanking you, outsiders. The pressure you have imposed... has at long last compelled me to confront my final... weakness.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Bronya, throughout your life, I have never forced you to submit to my will. You have always, will always have a choice... as then, so now.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Choose, my daughter.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Madam Cocolia... I am grateful to you for raising me, and for allowing me the privilege of choice.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: But... I am sorry, mother. On this, our final occasion, I cannot stand with you.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You say that conceit and cowardice lie in the depths of human nature — perhaps you're right... desperation sheds light on the darkest recesses of the heart.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...But what about those simply struggling for survival, fighting for something better? I've witnessed their light on the front lines, in the Underworld... in places you have overlooked.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Our ancestors built this city — striving in the bitter snow to prolong our civilization. Even if this world is doomed to fall apart, we should allow humanity to pave the way to its final outcome...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Not hand over our fate to this seed of ruin!
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: We are guardians, mother! Chosen from among the masses! Our duty is to preserve the world built by humanity! We are not gods! We are not arbiters!
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You seek to crush human nature underfoot while masquerading as an... as an arbiter and a god! I cannot let you!
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: So... this is your choice. I understand, Bronya.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Pity... Such a pity that you will never see that resplendent world... Unable to free yourself from the shackles of your mind... You know what? You were supposed to be... the mother of the new world.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: The ground... it's shaking! What's happening!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Bad sign...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: The fate of this city... of Belobog... is sealed. Its future will unfold in our hands.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: And you... will become the foundation of the new world!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: ...Himeko, it's Himeko!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hello? Can you hear me? This signal is terrible...
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Himeko! You finally spared a thought for us!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What are you talking about — Welt and I have been up on the star rail missing you this whole time! You've got quite the Trailblazing expedition on your hands.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: So how does this big guy work...? Or more importantly — how do you stop him from working? Over to you guys, I guess!
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Listen to the power surge... sing...
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: The Stellaron's promise is the only hope for this world...
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Just as it dispelled the Antimatter Legion 700 years ago, so too will it wipe you from the face of this world!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: *vicious laughter* Humanity... so weak and foolish. Always overestimating their abilities.
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Let me bestow upon you... despair!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: The city is drowning in tears... The power of the Preservation is fading.
rows.speaker: Guardians' Will

rows.text: We could not defy the will of the Stellaron after all...
rows.speaker: Guardians' Will

rows.text: Yes... But we have no right to judge.
rows.speaker: Guardians' Will

rows.text: Ah, a believer, I see?
rows.speaker: Guardians' Will

rows.text: Is this... the universe?
But I was fighting Cocolia. Why am I here...?
...The last time I came here, I drew Nanook's gaze. Could it be...
The Fragmentum had been expanding for the past 700 years. There is no faith nor wealth left for our successors... only despair.
rows.speaker: Guardians' Will

rows.text: To see the home we vowed to preserve wither away... That in itself is torture. Not to mention the haunting whisper of temptation...
rows.speaker: Guardians' Will

rows.text: The day will come when even the strongest of wills cannot help but give in to such influence. It is only a matter of time before the Amber Lord forsakes us.
rows.speaker: Guardians' Will

rows.text: You...
rows.speaker: Guardians' Will

rows.text: You are but a stranger to us. And yet you seek to bond your destiny to ours...
rows.speaker: Guardians' Will

rows.text: So be it. What is there to lose when so much has already been lost...
rows.speaker: Guardians' Will

rows.text: Touch the light of the Amber, trailblazer. See if your will can attract THEIR gaze.
rows.speaker: Guardians' Will

rows.text: No... It can't be...
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: The will of Preservation has made its choice...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You know nothing of the plight of this world... nothing of the wait for its final end!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Even if we are doomed to destruction, we will go bravely, walking hand in hand into the darkness...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: No! That end won't come to pass while we're around!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The power of the Stellaron is with me...
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: You are but cinders of the Old World soon to become ashes!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: It's over...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Mother... Did you wake up from that dream...?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Wow... that was a tough trailblazing expedition. Dan Heng, [Trailblazer] — we made it! But, uh, what are we gonna do with the Stellaron? It's usually Mr. Yang who handles it...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I've informed Himeko and Mr. Yang already. They'll seal the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Nice! The crisis on this world is basically over, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...The storm still rages on.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Now that the Stellaron is sealed, the Eternal Freeze will slowly recede. The Fragmentum won't aggressively expand anymore, but nor will it disappear. Jarilo-VI has a chance to return to life, but it will take time...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It will depend on the efforts of the people here.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Thank you... all of you.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Don't be too hard on yourself.
What do you want to do now?
Can't think of anything funny to say...
Thank you [Trailblazer]... I—I'm fine. Don't worry.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: This victory is only the beginning for Belobog.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Hehe, start thinking, we're going to need all the humor we can get... At least the biggest hurdle is behind us.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: There is still much to do... The people will have felt the effects of the Engine of Creation. There are so many questions to answer, so many truths to reveal...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I don't know whether I can get the people to accept all this...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Tell everyone the truth.
Cover up the truth...
Can I really do that...?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Tell everyone about Mother's true motives... about a lie perpetrated for 700 years...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: No... No, no way.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: You mean...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Use a lie to conceal a lie. But if I do that, then...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You have to, Bronya.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Seele?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I... I don't know how to explain it... but I don't think there's any other way.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: In the Underworld, we tell the kids "things will be better tomorrow." Everyone knows it's a lie, but it gets them to sleep with some hope.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Can you imagine the consequences if we told the people what happened here? They'd be devastated. If we can't trust the guardians, who — or what — can we trust...?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Mother died to preserve Belobog.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...What?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The visitors from beyond the sky told her the secret of the Stellaron. She knew that Alisa Rand, the first supreme guardian, had failed to destroy it...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...and yet she decided to challenge its power — a power beyond human comprehension. Supreme Guardian Cocolia sacrificed herself to dispel the dark clouds enveloping this city.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...From here on out, that's the "truth" the world will hear. What do you think?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: It keeps the hope of preservation alive, at least.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: It's logical... and hard to disprove.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Why do we have to lie? ...I'm abstaining — I like telling the truth. But... I get what you're trying to do.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Agreed — let's use this version.
A lie will always be a lie...
...Maybe we include some of the cool stuff we did?
Thank you for understanding, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I understand, but... I must protect those that believe in the Architects...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Sorry... I'll be sure to make it up to you.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: For many people, mother was an outstanding guardian... The whole truth will live on in my mind — all the mistakes, madness, evil, and dreams therein... I will be the one to carry that burden.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Now I must take over the duties of the supreme guardian... and discard my naive fantasies.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I'm sorry, Seele. Please protect this secret with me... till the end of our lives.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Say no more — I know what to do.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Thank you.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Well then, as promised, let's start rebuilding the bridge between the Overworld and the Underworld.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Seele, can you tell everyone in the Underworld that the Stellaron has been sealed? Tell them the blockade will soon be over... and they'll breathe freely again soon.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Of course, leave it to me — Nat's probably getting anxious about the delay.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: While you do that, I'll head back to the Administrative District. I need to tell Gepard... Serv— ah...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Are you okay!?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: What's wrong, Bronya? Do you feel sick?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm... fine. I need to... hurry...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: She's exhausted! Quick, we need to think of something... [Trailblazer], help me out here!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Seele, take Bronya back with you.
We'll go to the Underworld and pass on the message.
Right... I almost forgot, you're still wanted by the guards... I might be an Underworlder, but at least I don't stand out as much as you guys.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: That's settled then. I'll leave Nat to you. Remember to keep the secret — for Bron— No, for Belobog's sake.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: So, [Trailblazer], wanna tell us what happened back there? Don't think you can just reappear on the battlefield with a cool weapon in your hands and skip the story.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I saw Qlipoth the Preservation...
That's the second time I've sacrificed myself for you, March...
All of a sudden, I was infused with a great and terrible power...!
Uh... you drew the Amber Lord's gaze? Right at that moment? That's too much of a coincidence...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Um... thank you? That's not answering my question though...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Be serious! I really wanna know...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer] probably doesn't know what happened either. This wouldn't be the first time... Something similar happened when we faced the Doomsday Beast on the space station. Remember that glance from Nanook?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Originally, we thought it was because the Stellaron was linked to the Destruction, but now it seems to be more than that. We might need to speak with Mr. Yang to understand what's going on.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Let's focus on the business at hand first. We shouldn't disrupt Himeko and Mr. Yang while they're dealing with the Stellaron. Let's talk once we're back on the Express.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Mm, you're right, we need to finish what we started... Let's hurry up and find Natasha.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Are you alright? Are you hurt anywhere? Do you feel dizzy? Tired? Or...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...I don't know, Seele. I feel... cold... all over.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Isn't that normal? This place is freezing... *sneeze* Ugh...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I will not... let you!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: I... will save everyone...!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: In the name of every citizen of Belobog, I command you to rise... Engine of Creation!
No... No! Obey my commands! Obey me!
rows.speaker: Cocolia

rows.text: Let's get out of here before you catch a cold too.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Don't worry, I'm a tough cookie. Here, hold on to me... let's go.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Look! There's a big crowd around the clinic.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Do you think they felt the effects of the battle just now...? Let's go ask around.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Natasha! Oleg! Hope you didn't have to wait too long.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh! It's them!
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: You kids move fast! By the look on your faces, I assume you come bearing good news?
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Mm-hmm, you bet! You might not believe this, but we summoned up all our strength, and then...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Uh, maybe [Trailblazer] should do the talking. I'm no good at serious stuff — I'll probably say something I'll regret.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The guardian sacrificed herself to seal the Stellaron.
Do you feel like recounting the story, Dan Heng...?
We were there at the fight — we witnessed everything.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: "Sacrificed herself," huh... Sure. Yeah. That's the whole story...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The supreme guardian sacrificed herself to seal the Stellaron. We were there at the fight — we witnessed everything.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: "Sacrificed herself," huh... Sure. Yeah. That's the whole story...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Cocolia? In order to save Belobog, she... I see.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: So the massive tremors we felt earlier were a result of the battle, right?
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Yes, it was a hard-won victory.
We quite literally saved the world...
...Through patting yourself on the back!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Thank you. I can't even imagine what you've been through up there. I'm just glad everything turned out alright.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: What about Seele?
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Don't worry, she's alright! It took a big toll on Bronya, so Seele took her over to the Guards.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Good... I'm so glad you're all okay.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Now that Cocolia is no more, I guess our Silvermane girl is about to become the next supreme guardian?
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: She sees things through and doesn't go back on her word. The Underworld will thrive again under her watch.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Mm-hmm! Oh, we brought you a message from Bronya! Ahem, "The blockade will soon be lifted. The people of the Underworld will breathe freely."
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: "Breathe freely..." That's been our wish all along.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: March, Dan Heng, and [Trailblazer]... can I ask for your help again? I want to get this news out to everyone. It'll lift their spirits and bring them hope.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Count us in.
I can't wait to see their faces.
Thank you. Choose whoever you like. Wildfire will take care of the rest.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: We've gotten to know a lot of Underworlders... [Trailblazer], who do you think we should start with?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's start with the mining team over at the Great Mine.
Let's start with Hook and The Moles.
Let's start with Gertie.
Roger that — you can leave the rest to us. If everything goes smoothly... this should be Wildfire's final mission.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: ...Do you think the Great Mine was affected by our fighting on the surface?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's hope we didn't cause a collapse.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Look, it's Antonia! The miners and vagrants are all in the same spot.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I sure hope they're not arguing again... Quick, let's head over!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Here, take it. I'm afraid we're short on goods and materials right now.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: Oh, well we actually have enough for the moment. You hang onto it...
rows.speaker: Humble Vagrant

rows.text: Hey! Are you guys causing trouble again?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's you! Oh, no, no, you misunderstand...
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: There was a huge quake at the mine just now — part of it collapsed. If the vagrants here hadn't stopped to help, I doubt we'd have gotten everyone out in one piece.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: I was just discussing how to repay them. It's a shame the mining team is hard up right now.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: Wanna hear something really great?
I've got you covered.
Oh? To do with us? I'm listening...
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: Uh... can't we get Bronya to cover the bill?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ugh, can we focus? [Trailblazer], tell them the good news already!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You mean to say that... we're about to be reunited with the Overworld?
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: Are you serious!? This has... gotta be a dream. Good things... don't happen to us!
rows.speaker: Humble Vagrant

rows.text: Today they do! And you're not dreaming. If you don't believe us, pinch yourself!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: If things go back to the way they were 10 years ago... then the mining team can finally escape this poverty...
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: ...and you won't have to rely on the charity of others. We'll finally be living with the dignity we deserve.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: I... *sniff* *sob*
rows.speaker: Humble Vagrant

rows.text: Come on. Wipe your tears.
Let it out!
Thank you, outsiders, from the bottom of my heart! The mining team'll remember you as heroes... as will the rest of the Underworld.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: Please tell Natasha that we're ready to get back to work... If the cable car station can start operating again, we'll dispatch a mining representative to negotiate with the Architects.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: Hide-and-seek update... Astral Express crew — 2, The Moles — 0!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmph, celebrate while you can! Hide-and-seek is best of five, y'know...
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Anyway, enough about hide-and-seek. You came all this way to tell The Moles something, so spit it out.
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Telling the mining team and the vagrants about the victory...
Hehe... [Trailblazer], do you wanna do the honors?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Huh? What's wrong? Why aren't you saying anything?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hook, Julian...
rows.speaker: Alina

rows.text: Is our story that scary?
I wasn't expecting this reaction...
*sob*
rows.speaker: Julian

rows.text: ...H—Hey! Wipe your tears, Julian! You're second-in-command — no crying in front of grown-ups!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Hmph, you three listen up. Starting from today, you are The Moles' number one rivals!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Rivals...? Why the heck are we rivals now? What are you talking about?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Hook and Julian always wanted to defeat the villains on the surface and take back our homeland.
rows.speaker: Alina

rows.text: But it sounds like you grown-ups just stole their thunder, so...
rows.speaker: Alina

rows.text: Hmph! You think we're gonna accept defeat just like that!? One day The Moles will be the heroes of the Underworld and the Overworld! Then everyone will sit... sit...
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Sit up and take notice!
Sit down and shut up!
...Sit up and take notice, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ah! Yeah — sit up and take notice! I—I would've figured it out myself. I didn't need you to remind me!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: So that's why you were so silent! Hmph, if you wanna be as awesome as us, you better start training every day~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...And start listening to Natasha.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Training every day... listening to the old witch... Will that really make us as awesome as you guys? In that case... deal!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Julian, Alina, let's run back to the town! Training starts today!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Y—Yes boss! Understood!
rows.speaker: Julian

rows.text: Uh, Alina, I can... uh... give you a piggyback if you can't make it...
rows.speaker: Julian

rows.text: Why is everyone in such a hurry? I hope nothing's happened at the hotel...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We should take a look, maybe we can help.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I see Gertie! But who's that lying on the ground?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Quick, let's head over!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh my, this doesn't look good... Can you hear me? Are you okay?
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: H—He's still breathing! T—Try not to p—panic Aunt Gertie...
rows.speaker: Joshua

rows.text: Is everything okay? Wait, isn't that... Peak? Don't tell me he fell asleep in the middle of the road again.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You tell Gertie about the victory...
Oh, it's you three! Back in the Underworld so soon?
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Word must have gotten out that I was renovating the hotel today. Being the kind-hearted young man that he is, Peak came straight over and offered to help.
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: There we were hard at work, when all of a sudden the hotel started shaking... I got everyone outside as fast as I could, but I think Peak was hit by a ceiling tile...
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Are you sure he was "hard at work...?"
Quick, mouth-to-mouth resuscitation...
Look! Seems like he's coming around.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I... don't think that's necessary. Look, he's awake.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Huh...? Argh...
rows.speaker: Peak

rows.text: Peak, are you awake? Oh, thank goodness you're alright! Easy now, take your time...
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Argh, my back... I was having such a great nap, how did I...
rows.speaker: Peak

rows.text: A—Are you okay, bro? L—Let me take you to N—Natasha's clinic...
rows.speaker: Joshua

rows.text: Hey, look where he was lying. What is that?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's...
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: ...an old photo. I thought I lost this ages ago. How did it get...
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Aunt Gertie, isn't that you in the photo? And Old Goethe, too! You look so young!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't I know it. My distant cousin had only just taken over the family business at the time. He wrote me a letter inviting me to head up and take a look. It's been nearly 20 years already...
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: *sigh* I remember chatting in the hotel lobby and drinking tea. I wonder if we'll ever get another chance to do that...
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: ...Y'know, we've got some good news for you, haven't we, [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Is that true? Bronya, she... I—I can't believe my ears!
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Put your faith in Bronya.
You and Old Goethe will have the kettle on the stove in no time.
I... Hahaha! I don't know what to say! Turns out things aren't always lost forever. *sigh* It feels like better days are finally on the horizon!
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Thank you all so much for coming to tell me the good news. I haven't felt like this in a long time... We'll get plenty of guests staying at the hotel again once the passageway is open!
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: But there's no way I'm letting them set eyes on the old place looking like this... Oh, and we're gonna need to expand the menu. Oh dear. Action stations!
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Action... stations? Already? Ooh, um — ow, oww...! My head...
rows.speaker: Peak

rows.text: Please let Dr. Natasha know not to worry — we're all okay... You three will have to come and stay again once the hotel is fully renovated!
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: ...Mr. Yang put it nicely, but the reality is this: We sealed the Stellaron, but that's not gonna solve the problems on this planet...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: There I was getting excited to tell everyone the good news...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's the cruelty of a Stellaron. Still, compared with some of the other planets we've visited, at least this one has hope.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: So... should we tell everyone the deal?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We should tell Bronya when the time's right. Let's not dampen the spirit just yet.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Oh, is everyone alright? Thanks for your help.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Maybe next time we can send a group notification...
For you, anything.
Haha. Sometimes face-to-face communication is more meaningful, don't you think?
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: I'm flattered, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Now we just have to wait for the official news. I hope Bronya doesn't keep us too long.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Huh... do you think Svarog and Clara felt the effects of our battle with the guardian?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I think they'll be fine... Plus Svarog's devotion to Clara is even greater than his hostility to Wildfire. If you're worried, you could look for them over at the robot settlement.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Outssssiders... F—Friends of Clara.
rows.speaker: Perkins

rows.text: Hey Perkins!
Did Clara fix you?
How did you know that was Perkins...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Th—Th—Th—Thank you... for rescuing... Claaaara.
rows.speaker: Perkins

rows.text: Seems like Perkins picked up a stammer?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Its language module must have malfunctioned... Can you take us to Clara?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Outsiders... are f—friends of Clara... Follow me...
rows.speaker: Perkins

rows.text: You have visitors, Clara.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Ah! It's the variables!
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Do you have a license?
Does this thing have a good safety record?
Oh, uh, I'm afraid you might have to make an exception, {F#miss}{M#mr}. My license has expired, but then I haven't had the chance to go up and renew it for 10 years now...
rows.speaker: Cable Car Operator

rows.text: Another nickname for the collection...
Nice haircut, Svarog.
Time to take the kids out for some fresh air.
Not yet.
Brothers, sisters, ladies, gentlemen, boys, and girls of all ages — gather round! The cable car passenger service is about to restart!
rows.speaker: Cable Car Operator

rows.text: No problem, this car won't be leaving without you!
rows.speaker: Cable Car Operator

rows.text: So! Ready to climb aboard?
rows.speaker: Cable Car Operator

rows.text: Sure, why not.
Are you trying to start another fight...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: There was a huge shaking just now coming up through the ground. Mr. Svarog said it... must have been...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Recalculating... Conclusion: Engine of Creation. 97.66% probability.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Old friend of yours?
Telling The Moles about the victory...
Any other secret weapons you'd like to tell us about...?
The Engine of Creation was an immense construction machine created by the Architects. It was not built to fight.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Well whatever, we won... Thanks to that giant robot, we were finally able to take care of the Stellaron... and Bronya made a promise — the Underworld and the Overworld will soon be reunited.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Which means that you, Svarog — uh... You won't have to worry about preserving the Underworld... for the time being.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: March, everyone... thank you so much! I wasn't sure you guys would be able to do it, but...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: But now... Mr. Svarog, what do you say?
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: You guys said you were travelers from other worlds, right? I want to be just like you... One day, I'm gonna go traveling to faraway places and make new friends.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: I know you will.
Your future is yours to decide!
Calculation result... update. Mission number 0001 — Preserve the Underworld — complete.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: That's our Bronya — quick as a flash!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: She certainly moves a lot faster than some people I know...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...If you haven't got anything nice to say right now, zip it!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You made it... I thought you were about to miss out on a moment of history.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: No way! After all our hard work, how could we miss out on the final celebration? Right, [Trailblazer]?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'll go sit at the children's table.
The smell of freedom's in the air...
Haha, I don't know how much of a celebration we'll be having... but I know Hook and Clara will be pleased to sit with you.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Hehe, I smell it too.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: For Oleg and I, not to mention the other adults, reopening the passageway means rediscovering old ways of living — a return to "normality..." Survival is no longer the top of the agenda...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: But for the children who were born into this era, who grew up in this isolation... this will be a new life altogether.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: ...Once you've tasted freedom, it's difficult to accept a life of separation and isolation. Those of us whose childhoods were marred by tragedy... we must strive to do better for the next generation.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: I'm sorry, here I am talking your ear off again. This is a day to remember. We should welcome it with smiles.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: If you have time, talk to the folks here — every one of them will tell you about their excitement. Then, when you're ready... let's "go home."
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: It's been more than ten years. I can finally see my little girl again...
rows.speaker: Expectant Gentleman

rows.text: She must have graduated by now. I hope she found a good job — government administration or legal consulting, perhaps...
rows.speaker: Expectant Gentleman

rows.text: Please, Amber Lord, anything but those terrible magazine publishers! She's always liked to read those pointless things...
rows.speaker: Expectant Gentleman

rows.text: Mommy, what do children in the Overworld dress like?
rows.speaker: Alina

rows.text: Mommy doesn't know either, sweety — the Overworld is different from here. Their fashion is always changing, I don't know what's popular these days...
rows.speaker: Dunya

rows.text: Then... will other children laugh at me when we go up?
rows.speaker: Alina

rows.text: Don't be silly, that won't happen — mommy's gonna buy you some pretty new clothes as soon as we're on the surface.
rows.speaker: Dunya

rows.text: ...Deal! Thanks, mommy.
rows.speaker: Alina

rows.text: The Guards... they m—moved so q—quickly... don't you think it's a little f—fishy?
rows.speaker: Joshua

rows.text: I... I think it's hard to believe, but I've met that young lady Bronya. We didn't talk much, but she felt trustworthy to me.
rows.speaker: Elaine

rows.text: I don't really know what kind of person the new guardian is, but I heard the three outsiders are on good terms with her.
rows.speaker: Fidora

rows.text: Those three are really capable people. If they believe the Guards, then there's no reason for us not to.
rows.speaker: Fidora

rows.text: I g—guess...
rows.speaker: Joshua

rows.text: It's over, we're doomed...
I haven't even written my will yet!
What are you so worked up about?
It's not like we have much to will to anyone in the first place.
What was that shaking just now?
I thought the whole building was about to collapse...
The ground just kept on shaking...
Was it the Fragmentum?
Was it an earthquake?
No, it couldn't have been an earthquake...
What about an avalanche?
Eh, not an avalanche either...
Then could it be the end of the world?
Maybe...
Maybe next time we can send a group notification...
Fidora's right. They saved lots of people at the mines... I think they can be trusted.
rows.speaker: Elaine

rows.text: Finally... Finally I can get back to supervising the cable cars! I thought I'd spend the rest of my life in those mines...
rows.speaker: Cable Car Operator

rows.text: We did make a promise...
Ah, it's you! The liberators of the Underworld! You're the first passengers we've had since being sealed off — it'll be my honor to get you to the surface in one piece!
rows.speaker: Cable Car Operator

rows.text: We did all we could. Now it's a matter of time...
Does this count as false advertising?
Relax, relax! In all my 20 years on the job, there were only ever, uh... Anyway, none of them were serious!
rows.speaker: Cable Car Operator

rows.text: *cough* So! Ready to climb aboard?
rows.speaker: Cable Car Operator

rows.text: Ah, it's Gepard! Is he here to meet us?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: He's still on duty. Huh, he must have recovered quickly.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Let's go say hi.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Welcome back to the Administrative District, Trailblazers.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Trailblazers... first time anyone's called us that on this planet!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The Architects think it's only right that we should address you properly. "Outsiders" is hardly fitting anymore.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: ...Please allow me to apologize again for what happened in the restricted zone. You were only trying to help... I should've trusted Serval's judgment.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: You were just doing your job.
Your sister knows what's up...
Ha! Didn't expect to get wrecked, huh?
Thanks for understanding.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: I'll keep that in mind, thanks.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: You are excellent fighters. I'd love to have you provide training for the Guards, but I know you have places to be.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Lady Bronya's inaugural address will begin soon. She asked me to pass on her invitation to you.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Huh? That's sooner than I expected. Is she well enough to...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Not really... But Lady Bronya insisted on delivering the speech as soon as possible. She wants the people to understand what happened.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: The address will be held at Everwinter Monument. I hope the three of you can find time to attend.
rows.speaker: Gepard

rows.text: Look! There's a crowd gathering over there. Is the address starting soon?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Looks like it. Bronya hasn't arrived yet, though. Let's find somewhere to wait.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Wow! Did you see that, Clara? A super suuuper big steel monster just ran past!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: I don't think that's a monster... Mr. Svarog's database has information about it. It's called... hmm, I can't remember.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Don't worry about the name! The important thing is I saw what it can do — it has a huuuuge appetite and swallows people whole!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: And it just so happens to be The Moles' next target, hehe... We'll defeat the iron monster and save the people in its tummy!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Um... I don't think that's how it works...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: It's been more than a decade... I'm so glad to see you in the hotel lobby again, Mr. Goethe.
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Unbelievable... feels like it was just yesterday that I was showing you around the hotel all those years ago. I'm too old to remember a lot of things... but that day I remember clearly as ever.
rows.speaker: Old Goethe

rows.text: Since the passage between the Overworld and Underworld has opened up again, it's about time we shared some tips with each other, hotel manager to hotel manager.
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Of course, of course! I was worried before that after losing customers from the Overworld you would go out of business... but your establishment is still alive and well, all thanks to your superb management!
rows.speaker: Old Goethe

rows.text: You flatter me, Goethe! My hotel is getting refurbished. I'll be sure to invite you to visit again when the work is all done.
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: I don't know if you've ever had that feeling, [Trailblazer]... When you stop and look back on the things you've done, and wonder at all the obstacles you've overcome, the strength you've displayed...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: And then you start to doubt yourself, and wonder if you've lost that drive... If everything were to happen again, would you still stand strong?
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: I know the feeling.
I don't quite understand what you mean.
You do? Good... I mean, it's good to know someone in this world feels the same way as me.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: And that's not surprising — you're different from others. You seem to radiate a confidence most people don't have.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: I haven't been able to sit back once over the past ten years — a moment's negligence could have brought Wildfire crashing down... and the Underworld would've been beyond saving.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Staying vigilant wasn't the issue... it was the not knowing whether I'd ever be able to let my guard down again...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: No matter what anyone says, I believe your arrival was the reward for my long vigil. Thank you, Trailblazer.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: U—Uh, excuse me... are you Captain Oleg?
rows.speaker: Nervous Silvermane Guard

rows.text: ...Huh? I didn't think anyone would still remember my name after all this time.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Telling Bronya about Welt's observations...
Of course we remember! Every young guard knows about your courageous exploits!
rows.speaker: Nervous Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Oh? Which ones might they be? The time I finished off that rampaging prowler with just three bullets? Or when I defended the outpost from monsters for six days straight without food or water?
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: I haven't heard of either of them actually... But I'd love to hear all about them!
rows.speaker: Nervous Silvermane Guard

rows.text: Hahaha, sure! In which case, I'll cut my walk short and tell you all the grisly details...
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Sasha! My Sasha, is that you?
rows.speaker: Expectant Gentleman

rows.text: Dad! — by the Amber Lord, I thought I was never going to see you again!
rows.speaker: Tearful Woman

rows.text: Praise the Preservation, my child. Praise THEIR leniency... And who's this little one?
rows.speaker: Expectant Gentleman

rows.text: Here, Barry... say hello to grandpa!
rows.speaker: Tearful Woman

rows.text: Here we are, Everwinter Monument! Photo time!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, Pela and Hook are here too? Let's make sure we get them in the background!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Hello grandpa!
rows.speaker: Innocent Child

rows.text: My grandson... Is this my grandson? *sob*
rows.speaker: Expectant Gentleman

rows.text: Whoaaaa! So much ice! But it's warm here... aren't you Overworlders worried it'll melt?
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Not at all. It may look like ice, but it's actually a monument carved out of Geomarrow crystal.
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: Ah, Geomarrow! It's a shame daddy isn't here — He'd find a buyer for it and sell it for big bucks!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Uh... How do I explain... This particular piece of Geomarrow is definitely not for sale...
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: Have a look! I took a photo of everyone.
A "photo?" What's that? Hook wants to see it!
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: I must remind you that taking photos of others without gaining their permission violates Belobog public security ordinance number...
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: ...Wait, that's a nice picture! And... it's crystal clear.
rows.speaker: Pela

rows.text: Wow! Photos are awesome! ...Can Hook have it?
rows.speaker: Hook

rows.text: Hee-hee, you like it? It's yours. A farewell gift from us.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Who's there? Didn't your parents tell you to knock before—
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Ha, it's you three! Come on in! I was just talking to Clara about you.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: How have you been, {F#big sister}{M#big brother}? Miss Serval's workshop is amazing — there are all kinds of things... I like it here a lot!
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: "Miss Serval..." Clara is such a well-mannered kid! Meanwhile, the Architects' children are still calling me "auntie" and making me feel old...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Sorry Dad, I wanted to introduce you to my husband too, but he can't get away from the publisher today.
rows.speaker: Tearful Woman

rows.text: That's okay, my child, we've got all the time in the... did you say "publisher"?
rows.speaker: Expectant Gentleman

rows.text: Hey, that's not your line! We're here to take a photo, remember?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Photo? ...This feels like one of my fan meet-ups, haha. Anyway, for you guys, I'd do autographs for free.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: "Photo..." Oh! I remember. When I was little, Mr. Svarog took a photo for me...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Over here, Clara! Wanna learn some cool poses?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...There's gotta be a better shot than this one!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Um... I was trying really hard not to blink...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: *sigh* We shouldn't have trusted an amateur...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Never mind, at least it's memorable... A little farewell gift from the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Huh...? You're leaving so soon?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: *sigh* I understand. Well, this photo will always be close to my heart. I'll make a copy for you too, Clara.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Th—Thanks Miss Serval! {F#Big sister}{M#Big brother} [Trailblazer], March, Dan Heng... Thanks for taking care of me. Safe travels.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: If you have time... please come back and visit me and Mr. Svarog.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Guards, formation!
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard Announcer

rows.text: Whoa, this must be it.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Citizens of Belobog, I kindly ask for your attention! Lady Bronya Rand's inaugural address will begin shortly. Please remain orderly!
rows.speaker: Silvermane Guard Announcer

rows.text: Bronya, we're back!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: March, Dan Heng, [Trailblazer]... it's wonderful you made it to the address.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You're overwhelmed by a sea of weariness...
Go to bed.
Walk around a bit more.
The Engine of Creation, Cocolia, an ethereal outer space, the gaze of Preservation... your fragmented memory of the battle forms a blurry and surreal montage.
In the midst of this frantic tapestry of events, you see the moment Cocolia perished with the Stellaron. A strange voice speaks to you in a hushed tone...
But the voice passes rapidly. You try to recall what you saw in those fleeting moments, but find no trace.
All of a sudden, you hear it again... a female voice in your ear...
"At the end of your journey, all that perplexes you and troubles you will resolve."
Did you get Himeko's message? It's time to go. The conductor will nag us again if we put the Express behind schedule.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yeah, yeah. Well, pack your souvenirs and stuff. Back home we go!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* But the beds here are so nice!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You poor thing! I'll go check the lunar calendar — today might be unlucky.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Copycatitis still has no cure I see.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Morning, [Trailblazer]! How did you sleep? I'm full of energy myself!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Sorry, I know the invitation was very last minute... but I needed to get the news out as soon as possible. The longer people waited, the more rumors started to swirl. The situation risked spinning out of control.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Are you fully recovered?
Was Seele not there for the address?
Here we are at last... *sigh* It's sad to say goodbye.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Nothing lasts forever. You'll stop feeling sad the moment you set foot on the Express.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hey, I'm not that heartless y'know...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yes, I'm fine now. Don't worry.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: My mother... she tried to force the voice of the Stellaron into my head... It was a terrible feeling. I don't know what would've happened if you hadn't shown up.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: She was there. She just made sure no one could see her.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Seele is still new to the vastness of the Overworld — she feels uncomfortable in a big crowd... I'll help her adjust to life here.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: That was some speech, Bronya! If I had to talk like that in front of a huge crowd, I'd be shaking head to toe!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It was all just a bunch of palatable lies. I hope you never have a similar experience, March.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The part about preserving the seed of civilization was real.
On a scale from 1 to 5, how would you rate this journey...
It's what you do as a leader that matters.
Sometimes people need to hear white lies.
Mm... I'd prefer to be honest with the people... but I also want to preserve their hope.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Dan Heng, wanna... talk about Mr. Yang's findings?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Mm, allow me to explain.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Which means the Fragmentum has already taken root by this point. Even though the Stellaron is sealed, we won't be able to reverse the damage immediately...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Stellarons are terrible things.
Sorry, we promised you...
I know. Our ancestors wouldn't have risked using one if they'd had other ways of avoiding calamity.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: No... No need for apologies.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You've gone out of your way to save this world. [Trailblazer], you nearly lost your life. I have no right to ask for more.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Besides, I agree with Mr. Yang. Ultimately, the fate of Belobog is in the hands of its own people...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: We will find a way to root out the Fragmentum.
*yawn* ... That's enough sightseeing and photo-taking to last me a while...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Time to head back to the Goethe Hotel for a good night's sleep!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...We can sleep when we're back on the Express.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Not so fast! Last time we were here, that evil Madam Guardian interrupted us before we'd gotten the most out of our luxury suites... Don't you think we should make up for it?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Come onnnn! Himeko and Mr. Yang are grown-ups — I'm sure they'll cope without us for one night.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Besides, don't you want to chit-chat with the locals now that Belobog is full of life again? I know I do!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The Astral Express will do everything within our power to help.
In that case... as a leader, I must give you a promise of the same weight.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: We will hold out with everything we have until the day you Trailblazers return. Even if it takes another 700 years, the children of Jarilo-VI will look up to the sky with hope in their hearts.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: So long, my friends. May the Preservation bless your journey.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Congrats, [Trailblazer]! That was one heck of a first trailblazing expedition!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Worth celebrating, I'd say.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Two point five. Five!
rows.speaker: Dan Heng and March 7th

rows.text: ...What!? That run-of-the-mill, huh?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: My scoring criteria are different from yours.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Ugh! Anyway, we should be asking [Trailblazer]... Any thoughts you want to share?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Time for a nap...
I feel like I could fight a hundred more monsters!
What will the next adventure be like?
Wait, what? No way — we're about to leave and I've hardly got any decent photos.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Come on, let's go back to the Administrative District and hang out for a bit longer!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's the spirit! Come on, we should take some more photos before we head back to the Express.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's go! One more round in the Administrative District!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Equally unforgettable, I'm sure. Anyway, don't worry about the future — live in the moment!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's go for one more round in the Administrative District! I wanna take more photos!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: If you walk with your head down and your heart full of fear, your steps will grow heavier and your spirit will suffer.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: But if you find something to look up to and move forward with hope, then your steps will grow lighter... and if you should fall, you'll be on your feet before you know it.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Thank you for teaching me this, Trailblazers.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The inauguration ceremony went very smoothly. I didn't expect so many Underworlders to come and listen to the address.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Everyone seemed supportive, too. Seems like Bronya made a pretty good impression on them.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Possibly. They always think ahead.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: If those two approve of Bronya, then everyone following Wildfire won't question her either.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: She wanted me to stand next to her, but I'm glad I stuck to my guns. Besides, I'm not sure I could handle that many people staring at me.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No doubt. I figured that out back in the Underworld.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Leave...? So soon? I thought you'd stay for a few more days — at least until everything had calmed down...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Ahh... I get it. People are waiting for you to go back so you can keep traveling, right?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Shame, I thought we'd have more time to discuss all the crazy things you guys like to talk about. Looks like that'll have to wait till next time.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...And before you say anything, there will be a next time. I know we'll meet again.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Bronya said she's willing to wait 700 years for us...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmm... Dan Heng, how long can humans live for?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Forever. But in that scenario, they can't be considered human anymore.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yikes! So serious! I was just curious.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Of course I was! I was just hidden in the crowd. I'm glad you didn't notice me — means I'm doing something right. I want to protect Bronya in my own way.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Here we are, Everwinter Monument! Photo time!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, Pela and Hook are here too? Let's make sure we get them in the background!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Maybe we could try for a cleaner composition for this one...
Maybe Natasha and Oleg helped promote her a little.
Were you there? I don't think I saw you.
She will be an outstanding leader.
We're about to leave Belobog.
Good idea. Let's show them the photos once we're done.
Oh, we haven't seen Serval since we got back! Let's head to the workshop.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Who's there? Didn't your parents tell you to knock before—
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Ha, it's you three! Come on in! I was just talking to Clara about you.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: "Miss Serval..." Clara is such a well-mannered kid! Meanwhile, the Architects' children are still calling me "auntie" and making me feel old...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Let's take a photo together!
Still looking to hire assistants for the workshop?
Hey, that's not your line! We're here to take a photo, remember?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Photo? ...This feels like one of my fan meet-ups, haha. Anyway, for you guys, I'd do autographs for free.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: "Photo..." Oh! I remember. When I was little, Mr. Svarog took a photo for me...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Over here, Clara! Wanna learn some cool poses?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Wow, that's pretty great! I wish the photographers at my shows had your skills!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Huh...? Am I really that short? I thought...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Don't worry! If you eat like Dan Heng, you'll be as tall as him one day! *stifled laughter*
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...I'll let that slip.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Here, keep it... a little farewell gift from the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...There's gotta be a better shot than this one!
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Bronya said she's willing to wait 700 years for us...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmm... Dan Heng, how long can humans live for?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Forever. But in that scenario, they can't be considered human anymore.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yikes! So serious! I was just curious.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Okay... Where to next?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, we haven't seen Serval since we got back! Let's head to the workshop.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Home, sweet home! Mr. Yang and Himeko must be bored given how long our train had to stay here.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Where's our next stop? I can't wait!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The previous Supreme Guardian...
...forbid us to work here.
That girl was always paranoid since she was little...
Bronya is far more optimistic.
These dusty papers...
All requires the signature of the Supreme Guardian.
How could there be so many?
But Madam Cocolia...
...Gertie? It's Gertie, right?
Mr. Goethe! Long time no see!
What a spacious lobby...
My mother lived here as a child, you know.
So can Alina stay here too?
Yes, let me check with mother about the price...
Oh, you're from the Underworld?
That's right, born and raised.
Is something wrong?
No, it's just surprising...
After all, you are very dignified in your speech.
How would you rate my performance?
I'd say it's a solid five stars.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Piece of cake.
Confidence goes a long way.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Can I skip the next mission and get some rest?
*chuckles* And miss out on a great adventure? I don't think you'd like that.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Get some rest on the Express. Jarilo-VI was not an easy ride.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Um... I was trying really hard not to blink...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: *sigh* We shouldn't have trusted an amateur...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Maybe we could try for a cleaner composition for this one...
Good idea. Let's show them the photos once we're done.
Never mind, at least it's memorable... A little farewell gift from the Astral Express.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Huh...? You're leaving so soon?
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: How have you been, {F#big sister}{M#big brother}? Miss Serval's workshop is amazing — there are all kinds of things... I like it here a lot!
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: *sigh* I understand. Well, this photo will always be close to my heart. I'll make a copy for you too, Clara.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Let's take a photo together!
Still looking to hire assistants for the workshop?
If you have time... please come back and visit me and Mr. Svarog.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: *yawn* ... That's enough sightseeing and photo-taking to last me a while...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Time to head back to the Goethe Hotel for a good night's sleep!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...We can sleep when we're back on the Express.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Not so fast! Last time we were here, that evil Madam Guardian interrupted us before we'd gotten the most out of our luxury suites... Don't you think we should make up for it?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Come onnnn! Himeko and Mr. Yang are grown-ups — I'm sure they'll cope without us for one night.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Besides, don't you want to chit-chat with the locals now that Belobog is full of life again? I know I do!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I received Bronya's message before the inauguration ceremony. She told me everything that happened north of Belobog — about the Stellaron, and Cocolia's sacrifice...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: But...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: ...But?
Th—Thanks Miss Serval! {F#Big sister}{M#Big brother} [Trailblazer], March, Dan Heng... Thanks for taking care of me. Safe travels.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Uhh... Just listen to Bronya.
...Honestly, I feel that girl is hiding something from me. I knew Cocolia well, and she was never one to suddenly change her mind.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: *sigh* Don't worry, I won't dig too deep. I know Bronya must have thought long and hard before deciding what to make public.
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: I just... feel a bit empty now that we've lost the Stellaron — I spent a long time pursuing it, after all...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: As for Cocolia, the best side of her will live on in people's memory. That's not all bad...
rows.speaker: Serval

rows.text: Miss Serval is cool, strong, and... carefree...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: I want to be like her when I grow up so I can protect everyone... and protect Mr. Svarog!
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: I'm full of energy myself!
I dreamed about Sampo...
It's time we went home!
Aw, it was a close thing alright! Good thing it dawned on me: Hey, Sampo doesn't have to be a protagonist, right? The likes of us are better suited to... shadowy comic relief, huh?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Turns out the Astral Express crew is more fun than I expected! You liked it? Really? Haha, told you so!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: ...No no, I'm in no hurry to leave. What? Oh, Epsilon? Pff. What fun can you get out of a giant vanity fair like that? "True happiness always entails the manifestation of the dignity of mankind..." Now that's a quote I live by.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Leave Jarilo-VI and return to the Express.
I want to have one last look at this world...
Well, bye for now. Send my regards to the guys and girls in the tavern. Oh, and don't forget to say that Sampo Koski will catch them for the next one. Time to make my curtain call.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: To you, my dear audience, I dedicate my performance... I wonder, did I bring a little more joy into your lives?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: ...You don't have to answer that — but if the answer is no, then you'll break my heart.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: We should be getting back to the Express. Time to find March and Dan Heng.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Morning, [Trailblazer]! How did you sleep? I'm full of energy myself!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm full of energy myself!
I dreamed about Sampo...
It's time we went home!
...Copycatitis still has no cure I see.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You poor thing! I'll go check the lunar calendar — today might be unlucky.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* But the beds here are so nice!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Did you get Himeko's message? It's time to go. The conductor will nag us again if we put the Express behind schedule.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yeah, yeah. Well, pack your souvenirs and stuff. Back home we go!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *chuckles* And miss out on a great adventure? I don't think you'd like that.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Confidence goes a long way.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I'd say it's a solid five stars.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Here we are at last... *sigh* It's sad to say goodbye.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Nothing lasts forever. You'll stop feeling sad the moment you set foot on the Express.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hey, I'm not that heartless y'know...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: How would you rate my performance?
Piece of cake.
Can I skip the next mission and get some rest?
Leave Jarilo-VI and return to the Express.
I want to have one last look at this world...
Welcome home, you three.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Himeko, Mr. Yang! Team Trailblaze, back from duty! Mission one: Accomplished!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *chuckles* Although Welt and I didn't get the chance to go with you, I can tell you worked hard to bring things back to normal. Well done, everybody. And especially you, [Trailblazer]. I heard a lot of good things about you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Get some rest on the Express. Jarilo-VI was not an easy ride.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Pom-Pom is of the opinion that we should leave as soon as possible to avoid potential resurgences of the anomalies we experienced earlier. Himeko and I agree.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: ...Which means we need to decide where our next destination is, soon.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That's right.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: That's the path of the Nameless, I presume? Always on the road, always trailblazing...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Okay... Where to next?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I—I'm not complaining by the way! One adventure after another, that's exactly what I signed up for!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Looks like March has fallen in love with the way of the Nameless. That's good to hear.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You can head back to your rooms for some rest, or stay here and make yourselves a cup of coffee, whichever you like.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I'll head back to my room then.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: *sigh* There I was thinking this guy would gradually open up...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *chuckles* We need to give him some time, March. I think he treasures the time spent with you guys.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: [Trailblazer], about your battle against the Supreme Guardian and the whole Stellaron situation, you must have a lot of unanswered questions, I suppose?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: While you were away, Welt and I did some research and came to some interesting conclusions. Let me know if you want to ask about anything.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Home, sweet home! Mr. Yang and Himeko must be bored given how long our train had to stay here.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Where's our next stop? I can't wait!
rows.speaker: March 7th
